title: The Lion, the Bear and the Fox
summary: A lion and a bear found a slain fawn in the forest at the exact same moment. Both claimed the prize, and neither would yield a single scrap to the other....
keywords: the lion, the bear and the fox
full_text:
A lion and a bear found a slain fawn in the forest at the exact same moment. Both claimed the prize, and neither would yield a single scrap to the other.

They engaged in a terrible duel: teeth clashed against claws, blood flowed, and they tore each other until both collapsed upon the grass, bruised, bleeding, and too exhausted to lift a paw or move a muscle.

A fox, who had been watching the battle from behind a bush, trotted casually into the clearing. Seeing both titans incapacitated, he picked up the fawn between his jaws and walked off into the thicket at his leisure.

The dying fighters watched him depart, sighing in bitter sorrow: "How tragic our folly! We tore each other to pieces, only that a cowardly rogue might feast upon the fruit of our toil!"
moral: When two mighty contenders tear each other apart, a cunning onlooker steals the prize.
